tasks.short: Handle questions and problems between site managers and employees about contracts and daily work.

today.trigger: A site manager or employee raises a contract question or a workplace problem by phone, Teams, mail, or on the floor in Rotterdam, Tilburg or Venlo.
steps: Hear the question and work out whether it is a contract point, a CAO point, or a conflict between people.
Look up the person in AFAS Profit and the transport CAO, the warehouse CAO, or the policy on SharePoint.
Talk with the manager and, where it affects the employee, with the employee.
Say what the contract allows and agree a way to settle the problem.
Write the outcome in mail and, when it matters later, in the AFAS file.
drudgery: Hunting the right article in the correct CAO.
Rewriting the same explanation for another site.
Reconstructing the last answer from old mail.
Chasing two people who are on different shifts for one conversation.
today.time_sinks: Most of the lost time is searching, rewriting and waiting for people, wrapped around a conversation that itself cannot be skipped.

lenses.faster: The contract summary, the right CAO article and two similar past answers are on one page before the conversation, so the search and the rewrite drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A Teams or Outlook question from a manager opens that brief on its own. The conversation still waits for the HR business partner.
lenses.ambitious: At a tenth of the effort, every shift lead gets a same-day written position on ordinary contract questions, and repeated floor problems are visible before they become grievances.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss digging through SharePoint and old mail. The part people value, settling a real problem with the manager and the employee, stays.
lenses.options: Each brief offers three routes: apply the clause as written, use room the CAO already gives for a local arrangement, or escalate to the HR director or the works council, with the risk of each.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner maintains the checked answer library and the rule for which questions must come to a person, and handles the cases the rule sends up.
reach: Routine contract lookups that now land with the HR administrators.
Offer-clause questions a recruiter would otherwise escalate.
A payroll check before a manager promises a payment the CAO will not support.

tasks.human_edge: Judging what the conflict actually is, whether the floor will accept the outcome, and when the works council or the HR director must be involved. The HR business partner remains accountable for what Noordhaven tells an employee about their contract.
tasks.pattern_why: The result is a problem settled between people, so the HR business partner stays in the lead. The software prepares the file, the clause and a draft position, and the person conducts the conversation and decides.

in_practice.trigger: A manager's Teams or Outlook message, or a note taken on a floor visit, opens a case.
steps: Classify the question as contract, CAO, workplace conflict, or flex-worker terms.
Load the AFAS contract summary, the matching CAO article and similar approved answers.
Draft a short position in plain Dutch with two or three options.
The HR business partner talks with the people involved and edits the draft.
The HR business partner sends the answer and files the approved wording.
in_practice.human_gate: Nothing is told to the employee and nothing is written into the personnel file until the HR business partner confirms the interpretation.
data_needed: Employee group, site, contract hours and contract type from AFAS.
Current text of both CAOs and the company policies, with version dates.
Approved past answers, with names removed.
Whether the person is Noordhaven staff or employed by a staffing agency.
in_practice.logs_to: A short note on the employee in AFAS Profit, and the approved wording in a SharePoint answer library.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can summarise a mail thread and draft a reply from files the user already has in SharePoint.
AFAS Profit holds the employment contract, hours and absence record the HR business partner looks up today.
A library of approved Dutch answers, each tied to a CAO article, can serve repeated questions. Building that library is ordinary document work plus retrieval.

A tool that reads employee questions together with the personnel file can require works-council consent as a personnel system, and a tool that steers employment outcomes can fall in the EU AI Act high-risk employment category.

risks: A draft quotes the wrong CAO and the employee treats it as Noordhaven's position.
Local site practice differs from the written policy, so a fluent brief is neatly wrong.
Illness questions pull health data into a mailbox or a model the privacy officer has not accepted.
Logging every question becomes staff monitoring the works council has not agreed.
An answer written for Noordhaven staff is applied to an agency worker, whose employer is the agency.
research_questions: What share of these contacts are repeat questions with a written answer, and what share are disputes that need a conversation?
Are both CAOs and the contract templates on SharePoint the same versions payroll uses, including the latest amendment?
How often is the HR business partner's answer later corrected by payroll, compensation and benefits, or the HR director?
Is Microsoft 365 Copilot licensed in the tenant, and has the works council taken a view on tools that read employee questions with the personnel file?

tasks.short: Explain policies, both CAOs and the rules when managers or employees ask.

today.trigger: A manager or employee asks what a policy, a CAO rule, or a legal requirement means for their situation.
steps: Hear the question and identify the employee group and site.
Search SharePoint for the policy and the correct CAO text.
Check with payroll or compensation and benefits when money or hours are involved.
Write an explanation in plain Dutch that a shift lead can use.
Send it by Teams or mail and rarely file it anywhere others can reuse.
drudgery: Re-reading the same policy several times a week.
Working out which of the two CAOs applies.
Rewriting the same answer in simpler words for the warehouse.
Finding out whether a CAO amendment has already replaced the PDF on SharePoint.
today.time_sinks: The time goes into finding the current text and rewriting an explanation that has been given before.

lenses.faster: The employee group, the applicable paragraph and a plain-Dutch draft are ready together, so the search and the rewrite shrink to a check.
lenses.autonomous: A question that matches an approved answer, for the right CAO group, can be returned with the source paragraph without a fresh meeting. Anything uncertain waits.
lenses.ambitious: Every employee and shift lead can get the current rule the same day, in language the floor can use, and the company can see which rules cause the most confusion.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss typing the leave rule again. What remains is the hard reading, where the text does not cover the case and the HR business partner has to decide what Noordhaven will say.
lenses.options: Where a clause has two defensible readings, the draft shows both and states which reading payroll can actually process.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner edits the policy and the approved answer when questions show the text is unclear, and takes the gap to the HR director or the works council.
reach: First-line policy answers now given ad hoc by payroll and by compensation and benefits.
Certificate-rule answers that currently wait for a learning and development specialist.
The plain-language version of a policy the HR director would otherwise rewrite by hand.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what the rule means when the text does not cover the case, and stopping a fluent draft from becoming a promise the CAO or the law will not support.
tasks.pattern_why: The question is unstructured, but the answer is checkable against a source paragraph and the person's CAO group in AFAS. Several lookups are required, and the explanation counts only after an HR business partner has approved it, or once that exact approval is already on file.

in_practice.trigger: A policy or CAO question arrives by Teams, Outlook, or a floor note.
steps: Read the person's group in AFAS and select the transport CAO, the warehouse CAO, or a company policy.
Retrieve the paragraph that bears on the question and draft a short explanation that quotes it.
A check rejects any draft that has no matching source text, or that concerns dismissal, illness, equal treatment, or an individual sanction.
The HR business partner approves, edits, or blocks the answer.
Approved answers are stored so the next identical question returns the same text and the same source.
in_practice.human_gate: No explanation is sent as Noordhaven's position until an HR business partner approves it. A later identical question may reuse that approval. Dismissal, illness, equal treatment and sanctions always wait for a fresh approval.
data_needed: The employee's CAO group, site and contract type.
Versioned policy and CAO texts the works council and payroll recognise as current.
A list of topics that may never go out on an old approval.
The privacy officer's decision on which employee data a drafting tool may read.
in_practice.logs_to: The SharePoint answer library, with the source paragraph, the approver and the date. The individual question is stored only if it belongs in the AFAS personnel file.

evidence.claim: Microsoft 365 Copilot can draft from documents stored in SharePoint and from the mail or Teams thread in front of the user.
A workflow can require that every quoted passage appears in the source document, and can refuse to send a draft that fails that check.
Choosing the wrong collective agreement is avoided by reading the employee group from the HR system before any text is selected. AFAS Profit holds that group.
Staff-facing assistants that store employee questions need an AVG purpose and, where they monitor staff, a works-council route. Employment uses also need an EU AI Act classification.

risks: The draft cites a real paragraph and still draws the wrong conclusion.
A CAO amendment is in force while the library still holds the old PDF.
The answer is legally tidy and still unusable for a shift lead on a noisy floor.
An old approval is reused for a dismissal, illness, or equal-treatment question.
Health or works-council matters are typed into a channel that stores them without a proper basis.
research_questions: In a one-month sample, how many questions are answered by pointing at an existing paragraph, and how many need a real interpretation?
Does AFAS reliably separate drivers under the transport CAO from warehouse staff under the warehouse CAO?
Will shift leads use a written Teams answer, given that many of them now walk up to the HR business partner on the floor?
Who is allowed to mark an answer as approved, and how quickly is the library updated after a CAO change?

tasks.short: Match people to open work on the three sites within contract and certificate limits.

today.trigger: A site is short of people for a shift or a role, a long absence opens a gap, or a manager asks for flex workers.
steps: Ask the site what role, certificate and hours they need.
Pull headcount, contract hours and absence from AFAS, often via Excel.
Check forklift, VCA and food-safety completions in Studytube.
Look at the other sites and, if internal cover is thin, at the agency portals.
Discuss the options with the manager and sometimes with the employee who would have to move.
drudgery: Checking certificate dates one person at a time.
Reconciling AFAS hours with what the site manager believes the roster says.
Copying availability from three agency portals.
Rebuilding a similar shortlist every time a shift is short.
today.time_sinks: The slow part is assembling who is allowed to do the work. The conversation about who should actually be asked still takes the rest of the time.

lenses.faster: A shortlist of people who hold the certificate, have contract hours left and are not absent is ready when the request arrives, so the manual checks disappear.
lenses.autonomous: An unfilled shift request, a long absence, or a draft flex order starts the match overnight. Nobody is moved and no agency is called until a person approves.
lenses.ambitious: Every open shift is offered first to internal people who are allowed to do it, and flex is ordered only for the remaining gap. That is how cover should work, and today it depends on who has time to check.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the spreadsheet matching. The conversation about a fair move, with the manager and the employee, stays.
lenses.options: Each request shows internal redeployment, overtime inside CAO limits, and an agency order, with the cost and the effect on day-90 retention beside each option.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner sets the match rules for certificates, contract hours, travel between sites and fair rotation, and reviews the exceptions rather than building each list.
reach: The internal shortlist a site now skips by ordering flex directly in an agency portal.
A certificate gap sent to learning and development before the shift fails.
A view for the controller of agency hours that were available internally.

tasks.human_edge: Judging who can fairly be asked to change site or shift, and spotting when a proposed match is really a change of workplace, a contract change, or a labour-relations problem.
tasks.pattern_why: Hard constraints such as a valid certificate, remaining contract hours and absence can be applied from AFAS and Studytube by rules. Moving a person or placing a flex order still counts only after the HR business partner approves, because the decision affects people's work and the CAO.

in_practice.trigger: A site manager submits an unfilled role or shift, a long absence is recorded in AFAS, or someone starts a flex order.
steps: Read the role, site, required certificate and dates from the request.
Exclude people whose certificate is missing or expired in Studytube, whose contract hours are already full, or who are absent.
Rank the remaining internal people by site, fairness of recent moves and cost, and show the flex option separately.
The HR business partner checks the shortlist with the manager and, if a person must change site or shift, with that person.
Only the approved option is acted on: an internal assignment, overtime, or an agency order.
in_practice.human_gate: No employee is moved, and no flex order is placed, until the HR business partner and the site manager agree the match.
data_needed: Contract hours, site, role and a fit-for-shift absence flag from AFAS, without the medical reason.
Certificate name and expiry from Studytube for forklift, VCA and food safety.
Open shift or role, and any workplace fixed in the contract.
Agency worker identifiers and certificates, if the three portals can provide them.
in_practice.logs_to: The request and the approved choice, including who was eligible and why a person was not proposed, stored in SharePoint and summarised on the AFAS note where an individual is moved.

evidence.claim: Studytube records enrolments and completions for mandatory certificates, including forklift, VCA and food safety.
AFAS Profit holds contracts, planned hours and absence, which are the constraints on who can take extra work.
A rules list on those fields can produce an eligibility shortlist without a language model. The judgment of fairness stays with a person.
Systems that allocate tasks to individual workers can fall in the EU AI Act high-risk employment category, so a proposal with a human decision and a record is the cautious design.

risks: A shortlist is treated as an order to move someone, against the contract or without the works council where a relocation rule applies.
Health-related limits are either missing, so the match is unsafe, or processed without a lawful basis.
The same people are repeatedly proposed for the unpopular shifts because the fairness rule was never written.
Flex certificates and hours stay inside agency portals, so the internal gap is overstated and an order goes out anyway.
Ranking workers for tasks is the kind of use the EU AI Act treats as high-risk employment software.
research_questions: Who builds the weekly roster today, and does the HR business partner allocate people or only advise after operations has already decided?
What share of shortages is an expired or missing certificate rather than an empty seat?
Are flex workers' certificates and agreed hours visible from AFAS or Studytube, or only inside the three agency portals?
Will managers treat the shortlist as something they may reject, and is a change of usual site restricted in the contracts?

tasks.short: Advise site managers on hiring and on keeping people past day 90.

today.trigger: A site has open roles, a hiring round is stalling, or leavers before day 90 prompt a conversation with the site manager.
steps: Export the Recruitee pipeline and ask the recruiters what is stuck.
Pull starters, leavers and absence from the Power BI extract of AFAS, then finish the table in Excel.
Try to see which new hires finished week-one onboarding and who left before day 90.
Draft a note or a few slides for the site manager.
Sit with the manager and agree what will be done on hiring or retention.
drudgery: Reconciling a Recruitee hire with an AFAS starter by name.
Chasing exit reasons that were never entered.
Rebuilding the same site table every month.
Formatting slides from numbers that already sit in Power BI.
today.time_sinks: Reconciliation and slide-making take as long as the management conversation they are meant to support.

lenses.faster: Each site pack arrives with open roles, stage ages, offer acceptance, week-one onboarding and day-90 losses already compared, so the export and the slide build drop out.
lenses.autonomous: A role that passes the agreed time-to-hire limit, or a hire who leaves before day 90, opens a case note for the HR business partner. The advice itself still happens in the meeting.
lenses.ambitious: Every role family on every site has a retention practice that is actually run, with a buddy, the mandatory certificates in week one and a manager check-in, and the company can see which of those move the day-90 result.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the name-matching between Recruitee and AFAS. What people value is the conversation in which a site manager commits to a practice they will really run.
lenses.options: The briefing offers three programmes: clear the stalled pipeline, fix week-one onboarding, or change the agency mix, each with the expected effect on day-90 retention and the cost.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner owns the definition of productive at day 90 and reviews which programmes work, and stops assembling the numbers for each meeting.
reach: A challenge to the recruiters on roles that sit too long in a Recruitee stage.
Day-90 definitions the people analytics analyst can then keep in Power BI.
A shared cost-per-productive-hire figure with FP&A, using those same definitions.

tasks.human_edge: Choosing the programme a particular site manager will actually carry out, and holding the line that a fast hire who is gone before day 90 is a failure on the north star.
tasks.pattern_why: The task is advice to management, and the HR business partner stays responsible for the recommendation. The software prepares the site pack and the scenarios from Recruitee and AFAS; the person leads the conversation and chooses the programme.

in_practice.trigger: A monthly cycle, plus an immediate note when a role breaches the time-to-hire threshold or a hire ends before day 90.
steps: Combine Recruitee stage dates with AFAS start dates, site and employment status at day 90.
Add Studytube week-one completion for the mandatory certificates.
Draft a one-page site brief with three programme options and the small-number warning where a group is tiny.
The HR business partner edits the brief and holds the meeting with the site manager and, where needed, the recruiter.
The agreed actions and the definition of productive are written down for the next cycle.
in_practice.human_gate: No programme is presented as the HR recommendation, and no target is set for a site, until the HR business partner has signed off the brief.
data_needed: A shared identifier from accepted Recruitee offer to AFAS employee.
Stage dates, offer acceptance and open roles from Recruitee.
Start date, site, contract type, leaver date and absence from AFAS.
Week-one certificate completion from Studytube, and an agreed definition of productive.
in_practice.logs_to: The monthly site note on SharePoint, next to the written definition of productive at day 90.

evidence.claim: Recruitee stores vacancies, pipeline stages, interview feedback and offers, and can show how long candidates remain in a stage.
Power BI already refreshes overnight on an AFAS extract and can show starters, leavers and absence by site.
The north star, a hire who is productive and still employed at day 90, needs a join across Recruitee and AFAS that neither product holds as a single field.
Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint can produce a first deck from a structured note the HR business partner then edits.

risks: Recruitee and AFAS do not join cleanly, so the day-90 figure is wrong and the advice sounds certain.
A handful of leavers at Venlo, or in one role, is treated as proof that a programme failed.
Pressure to cut time to hire lowers the quality of hires and worsens the north star.
A retention bonus or a monitoring practice starts without the works-council route it needs.
research_questions: Is there a person identifier that links a Recruitee offer to an AFAS employee and to status at day 90?
How does Noordhaven define productive for a warehouse hire and for an office hire?
How much of these 92 hours is the management meeting, and how much is building the pack?
Which retention actions can a site manager take inside the CAO and without a new works-council trajectory?

tasks.short: Coach managers on interviews, appraisals and documenting a performance problem.

today.trigger: A manager has to interview, hold an appraisal, counsel someone, or document a performance problem and asks HR how to do it.
steps: Find the interview guide, appraisal form or warning template on SharePoint.
Explain the company procedure and what the file needs to contain.
Role-play the conversation or sit in on a hard one.
Review the manager's notes or letter before they are filed.
Point the manager at a course in Studytube when one exists, and often find that it is out of date.
drudgery: Searching for the current template.
Rewriting the same checklist for each new shift lead.
Cleaning up letters that mix gossip, health and the actual work problem.
Repeating basic interview training that the recruiters also give.
today.time_sinks: Rebuilding materials and repairing weak documents take the hours. The coaching conversation is the smaller, valuable part.

lenses.faster: A situation-specific checklist and a rehearsal brief are ready before the session, so template hunting and first-draft rewriting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: When a manager books an appraisal or an improvement meeting, or when Recruitee interview feedback is empty, a prep pack is added to the meeting. The coaching session still belongs to the HR business partner.
lenses.ambitious: Every new shift lead practises interviews and performance conversations before doing them alone, and the file is complete the first time. That is the standard a dismissal trajectory later depends on.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss rewriting the warning-letter structure. Coaching a manager through a conversation they find difficult is the part worth keeping.
lenses.options: The brief sets out three paths, coach on the job, a formal warning, or a supported exit, and lists what the file must contain for each and what must stay out of it.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner maintains the manager curriculum and the dossier standard, reviews a sample of files, and joins in person only when a case is heading toward a formal trajectory.
reach: Interviewer calibration that now sits only with the two recruiters.
A Studytube module maintained together with the learning and development specialists.
A review of warning letters before HR administration files them.

tasks.human_edge: Seeing whether this manager can hold the conversation fairly, and stopping a dossier that is incomplete, that contains health data, or that will not stand up in a later dismissal route.
tasks.pattern_why: The task is teaching and coaching managers, and the HR business partner has to see the person in front of them. Draft briefs, checklists and rehearsal outlines make the session ready; they do not replace it.

in_practice.trigger: A manager asks for help, or a calendar item for an interview, appraisal, or improvement meeting is created.
steps: Select the agreed procedure and the SharePoint template for that situation.
Draft a one-page brief: purpose, questions, what to write down, and what not to write down.
Add a short rehearsal script the manager can practise before the HR business partner session.
The HR business partner runs the coaching and edits the manager's letter or notes.
Completion of any standing module is recorded in Studytube, and the reviewed document is filed.
in_practice.human_gate: No warning letter, appraisal text, or performance plan is filed in AFAS until the HR business partner has reviewed it. A draft is never sent to the employee as the company's position.
data_needed: The current appraisal and warning procedure, including any version the works council has agreed.
Templates in Dutch at a reading level a new shift lead can use.
The manager's draft notes, with health data kept out of the performance file.
Recruitee interview-feedback fields where the training is about hiring interviews.
in_practice.logs_to: The reviewed document in the AFAS file when it concerns a named employee, and the training outline plus Studytube completion for the curriculum.

evidence.claim: Studytube can host a manager module and record who completed it.
SharePoint already stores the company's contract templates and can store the current dossier templates and checklists.
A rehearsal draft helps a manager practise and is a poor record of what was actually said. The filed document still needs a human review.
Microsoft 365 Copilot can produce a first draft of a checklist or a role-play from a SharePoint procedure the company already holds.

risks: A generated letter is harsher than the procedure allows, or it names health data.
Managers treat the draft as legal clearance for a dismissal file.
Practice notes about a named employee are stored as if they were the official dossier.
The Studytube module drifts away from the procedure the works council agreed.
A performance file and a Wet verbetering poortwachter reintegration file get mixed.
research_questions: Is there an appraisal and warning procedure the works council has already agreed?
What share of these hours is training, and what share is repairing a dossier after a conversation went badly?
Are the current templates in Dutch, at a reading level a new shift lead can use under time pressure?
Will managers complete a short Studytube module before they interview alone or start a formal performance trajectory?

tasks.short: Design how Noordhaven hears about working conditions and handles complaints.

today.trigger: Once or twice a year someone asks for a satisfaction survey, or a cluster of complaints shows the old route is not working.
steps: Draft questions in Excel or a mail, mostly aimed at people with a company mailbox.
Discuss the questions with the HR director and, when it is remembered, with the works council.
Ask site managers to give warehouse staff time to respond.
Read the comments by hand and group them.
Write or patch a complaint procedure and store it on SharePoint.
drudgery: Chasing responses from people who do not sit at a desk.
Cleaning comments that mix a working-condition point with a named grievance.
Rewriting the complaint procedure into policy language.
Rebuilding a survey that was not designed for night shifts or flex workers.
today.time_sinks: The hours go to chasing answers and rewriting a procedure. Little time is left to design a method the warehouse will actually use.

lenses.faster: A first questionnaire, a shift-friendly way to collect it, and a complaint-procedure outline are ready to edit, so the blank page and the policy formatting disappear.
lenses.autonomous: A spike in exits or verzuim at one site can propose a short pulse. Nothing is sent until the HR business partner takes the method to the works council.
lenses.ambitious: A complaint route that night shifts actually use, and a quarterly picture by site and by permanent versus flex, would be the first time this is done properly. Forty hours a year cannot produce that by hand.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss reminder mails and response chasing. Designing a fair procedure, and hearing what the floor says, is the work worth keeping.
lenses.options: Three collection methods are compared: a QR code in the canteen during paid time, a short pulse after onboarding, and a structured floor round, each with its response bias and its works-council implication.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner sets what may be asked, how small groups are protected, and how complaints are handled, then reviews whether night shifts and flex workers are actually reached.
reach: A survey design the people analytics analyst can run without inventing the questions.
A complaint-procedure draft for the works council and the HR director.
A link between complaint themes and the absence figures HR administration already tracks.

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether people on the floor and the works council can trust the method, and deciding which questions must not be asked at all.
tasks.pattern_why: The product is a method that has to be acceptable to the floor and the works council, so the HR business partner leads. Draft questions, a collection plan and a procedure outline remove the blank-page work.

in_practice.trigger: A planned review of the listening method, or a site signal such as a jump in exits or verzuim that the HR business partner decides to investigate.
steps: Draft a short questionnaire in Dutch, separate for warehouse shifts and office, with flex workers treated as a distinct group.
Propose how collection works on nights and weekends, on paid time, without using a company mailbox as the only door.
Draft the complaint route: where a complaint goes, who sees the name, and what never enters a personnel file.
The HR business partner edits this with the HR director and puts it to the works council before anything is sent.
After approval, the method, the questions and the suppression rule are filed for the analyst to run.
in_practice.human_gate: No survey is sent and no complaint procedure is published until the HR business partner and the works council have finished the route that applies.
data_needed: Any existing klachtenregeling and the date it was last agreed.
Headcount by site, shift and contract type, so small groups are not surveyed into identification.
The works council's position on staff surveys and complaint procedures.
A rule for whether agency workers can be asked, and by whom.
in_practice.logs_to: The method statement, the questions and the works-council correspondence in SharePoint. Individual complaint records stay in the channel the procedure names, not in the survey file.

evidence.claim: Microsoft Forms, as part of Microsoft 365, can collect questionnaire responses in the same tenant as Outlook and SharePoint.
Under the WOR, a complaint procedure and a system that follows staff behaviour are typical works-council consent topics. The exact route depends on the text Noordhaven agrees with its OR.
An email-only survey will miss a large share of shift workers and agency workers. Collection has to be designed around shifts and paid time.

risks: The survey becomes monitoring of named people, especially on a small night shift.
Comments identify someone after names are removed, because the team is small.
Flex workers are questioned although the agency employs them, or they are omitted and the picture is only permanent staff.
A low response rate is presented as the view of the warehouse.
Complaint text is later copied into a personnel file and used for another purpose.
research_questions: Is there a klachtenregeling today, and when did someone last use it?
What response rate do current surveys get from warehouse night shifts, from Tilburg and Venlo, and from flex workers?
Does the works council treat a new survey or a new complaint route as a consent file?
Do exit reasons, verzuim and existing complaints already show the same problems a new method would look for?

tasks.short: Prepare the satisfaction figures and the management slides.

today.trigger: A management meeting or a works-council meeting needs figures on employee satisfaction or working conditions.
steps: Export numbers from Power BI or from the survey spreadsheet.
Paste them into PowerPoint and rebuild last time's charts.
Write a few bullets that explain the movement.
Check the totals by hand against the export.
Send the deck to site management and sometimes a different cut to the works council.
drudgery: Copying figures from one file into another.
Rebuilding the same charts.
Checking that the slide matches the export.
Producing a second cut for the works council by hand.
today.time_sinks: Almost all of the 36 hours are formatting and reconciling. The judgment is a thin layer on top.

lenses.faster: The pack is filled from the same dataset as the dashboard, so export, paste and chart rebuild disappear.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh and a new satisfaction file rebuild the pack on a schedule. The HR business partner is told only when a rule flags it.
lenses.ambitious: Every site manager gets the same monthly pack, including shift and flex where the group is large enough, and the works council gets the cut it was promised. Today this is a thin deck a few times a year.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss formatting slides. Deciding what a real movement means, and what to do about it, stays with the HR business partner in the meeting.
lenses.options: The same pack can show site, contract type, and tenure under and over 90 days. Any cut under the size threshold is dropped rather than shown as a separate story.
lenses.altitude: The HR business partner owns the definitions and the suppression rules, and stops building the slides.
reach: The monthly production work that now sits with the people analytics and HRIS analyst.
One pack the HR director and the site managers can read beside the finance figures that already come from Power BI.
The agreed works-council cut, produced from the same run so the numbers cannot diverge.

tasks.human_edge: Deciding what a movement means, and what must be left out so a small team in Venlo or on a night shift cannot be identified.
tasks.pattern_why: The inputs are structured and the output is checkable: fixed cuts, fixed comparisons with last month, and a size threshold below which a group is hidden. Rules can fill the pack. A language model is unnecessary, and the HR business partner handles the packs the rules flag.

in_practice.trigger: The scheduled run after the nightly AFAS refresh, and the arrival of a new satisfaction file.
steps: Load the satisfaction file and the AFAS headcount cut from the same refresh date.
Compute the agreed views: site, contract type, and tenure under and over 90 days.
Suppress any group under the agreed size and flag that pack.
Flag a pack when a figure moves by more than the agreed amount versus last month.
Send unflagged packs to the named managers and file them. Hold flagged packs for the HR business partner.
in_practice.human_gate: A pack that suppresses a small group or shows a large movement is not sent until the HR business partner adds a note or withdraws the page. Ordinary packs go out on the schedule.
data_needed: The satisfaction responses with site, contract type and tenure, and no free-text names.
Headcount from the nightly AFAS extract on the same date.
The minimum group size agreed with the privacy officer and the works council.
The distribution list for site managers, the HR director and the works council cut.
in_practice.logs_to: The issued pack in SharePoint, stamped with the Power BI refresh date it was taken from, plus the HR business partner's note on any flagged pack.

evidence.claim: Power BI can refresh on a schedule from the nightly AFAS extract and hold a fixed report page with agreed filters.
A threshold that hides groups below a set size, and a comparison with the previous period, can be written as report rules without a language model.
Where a narrative deck is still required, Microsoft 365 Copilot in PowerPoint can build a first deck from the filed pack. The standard monthly pack itself does not need that step.

risks: A slide shows a group small enough to identify a person or a shift.
A templated sentence is read as a cause the figures do not support.
A deck exported on a different day diverges from the Power BI page.
The works council receives a different cut from the one it was shown in the method.
Warehouse responses are missing and the pack describes the office without saying so.
research_questions: Where does satisfaction data live today, and is any of it in the nightly extract Power BI already refreshes?
What smallest group size will the privacy officer and the works council allow on a page?
How many of these 36 hours are formatting, and how many are the meeting where the figures are discussed?
Will site managers read a Power BI page, which would remove the PowerPoint step?

role.altitude: The HR business partner stops answering, matching, coaching and reporting one case at a time, and instead maintains the rules those cases run on: the approved answer library, the match rules, the meaning of productive at day 90, and the manager standard. The three HR business partners then spend their time on exceptions, labour relations and on improving those rules across Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo.
reach: Routine contract and policy answers that now sit with the HR administrators.
Offer-clause questions and interviewer calibration that now sit with the recruiters.
Certificate gaps that block a shift, which today are visible mainly to the learning and development specialists.
The monthly people pack that the people analytics and HRIS analyst now assembles by hand.
An early check of whether a promise to a manager can actually be paid under the CAO, which payroll and compensation and benefits now discover later.
role.ceiling_note: These seven tasks are about half the role, roughly 800 hours a year per person. If the task estimates hold, about 350 of those hours come back per HR business partner, mainly from policy explanations, match lists and report preparation. Live conflicts, the works-council relationship, illness files under the Wet verbetering poortwachter, and any dossier that can end in dismissal stay with the three people, because they depend on presence and personal accountability. The ceiling is how many of those cases three HR business partners can carry on three sites, not how fast the software runs.
skills_to_grow: Writing approved answers and match rules that someone else can run, with a source and a review date.
Reading a Power BI page and applying a small-group rule before a figure is shown.
Taking a new staff-facing tool or survey through the works council and AVG before it is switched on.
Coaching managers so a performance file is fair, free of health data, and usable in a Dutch dismissal trajectory.
Comparing internal cover with an agency order using certificates, CAO hours and day-90 retention.
role.ambitious_version: The three HR business partners run hire-to-day-90 as a system for every role family on every site. Managers hire, appraise and document to a standard they have practised. A shift lead gets a correct answer on the right CAO the same day. People with a valid certificate and hours left in their contract are proposed before a flex order goes to an agency. The works council sees one agreed picture of working conditions, with small groups hidden. The HR business partners spend the week on the exceptions, on labour relations, and on correcting the rules when the floor shows the rules are wrong.
